## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One validator still allows passwords shorter than twelve characters, and that needs fixing: `app/invite.py:1` keeps `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8` while this PR raises the signup and reset validators to 12. That leaves the invite path below the new security policy. This review read every changed file, the untouched `app/invite.py`, `app/tokens.py` and `tests/test_invite.py`, and searched the repository for other password-length constants. The updated tests in `tests/test_reset.py` and `tests/test_signup.py` test both sides of the new boundary (11 rejected, 12 accepted). This review read those tests but did not run them.

## Changes
The PR raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` from 8 to 12 in `app/signup.py` and `app/reset.py`, and moves the boundary cases in their tests to 0, 8, 11, 12 and 13. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — Raise the invite validator minimum to twelve — An invited user who sets an 8-to-11-character password, such as `"x" * 8`, still gets through because `app/invite.py:1` keeps `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8` and `app/invite.py:5` checks `len(password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH`. This PR changes the same constant in `app/signup.py:1` and `app/reset.py:1` only, but the description says it "raises the minimum in the password validators". `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still expects `length >= 8`. — Accounts created through invites can still get passwords that break the twelve-character security policy this PR is meant to enforce, and the invite test will keep the old minimum in place. — Fix: Set `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12` in `app/invite.py:1`, and change `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` to the `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` form used in the other two tests.
